title: Does ChatGPT actually think? (in 60 seconds)
description: Is ChatGPT thinking or just predicting the next word? Thoma shows what a large language model really does, step by step, and where the real debate is.
pinned_comment: Be honest: do you think ChatGPT understands you, or is it just very good at guessing?

scenes.say: Does ChatGPT actually think, or is it just a really fancy autocomplete?
Let's poke it and see. First, it chops your message into tokens, little word pieces, and each one becomes a number.
Then billions of tiny dials, called weights, crunch those numbers in a neural network.
And out comes a score for every possible next word. The sky is... blue wins, so it writes blue. Then it does it again.
Here's the trick. To guess well, it learned that words with similar meanings sit close together, like a map of ideas.
But it has no fact checker. When it doesn't know, it still predicts something confident.

messages.text: Who won the 1890 Kerala chess cup?
Easy! Raman Nair won it in a famous final.

scenes.say: So is it thinking? Researchers honestly disagree. Some say prediction at this scale is a kind of reasoning.

visual.sub: Prediction at huge scale can look like reasoning

scenes.say: So which side are you on? Comment below. Thoma out!

visual.text: LLMs *predict the next word*, so well it looks like thinking.
